methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates WES, WGS, RNA-seq, and single-cell RNA-seq across 137 TETs (20 newly sequenced + 117 TCGA) with cross-species mapping to murine TEC atlases, and validates findings using independent public single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets, strengthening internal consistency. Statistical methods are appropriate (Wilcoxon, Fisher exact, log-rank, Cox proportional hazards, Benjamini-Hochberg correction for DEGs, permutation-based CIs for amplification timing) and GTF2I detection was carefully rescued via RNA-seq. Weaknesses include: functional IRS4 validation performed only in HEK293T cells rather than thymoma-relevant lines; WGS cohort for timing analysis is small (n=5); no formal power calculation; multiplicity correction not uniformly described across all exploratory comparisons; and the IRS4 >30 TPM threshold for survival appears post hoc without an independent validation cohort for the cutoff.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The design is a retrospective molecular classification/case series of a rare cancer combined with preclinical mechanistic validation, mapping to Oxford LoE 4 (case series/low-quality cohort with retrospective outcome correlation). Clinical relevance is substantial: a molecularly defined three-subgroup stratification could refine WHO histologic classification, whose interobserver reproducibility is noted as poor; IRS4 is proposed as a prognostic biomarker independent of Masaoka stage via Cox regression; and functional data show IRS4-high cells acquire resistance to IGF1R inhibition (linsitinib), with direct implications for a candidate therapeutic strategy. Immune checkpoint analyses nominating CTLA4/CD80-CD86 and IDO1 over PD-1/PD-L1 are actionable hypotheses for immunotherapy trial design in TETs.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is the most applicable standard given the retrospective observational cohort design, with REMARK elements relevant to the IRS4 prognostic analysis. Methods are detailed for sequencing pipelines, bioinformatics tools (versions provided for STAR, RSEM, Sequenza, BBKNN, Seurat, mixtools, fgsea, GSVA, etc.), and IRB approvals are documented. However, key STROBE/REMARK items are incompletely addressed: no explicit case-selection flow diagram, no pre-specification of the IRS4 cutoff, no sample size justification, limited reporting of missing data handling, and inclusion/exclusion criteria for the SNUH cohort are only partially described. The blinded manuscript includes TCGA re-use and a Supplementary Table S1 reference, but no explicit public repository accession for new SNUH WGS/WES/RNA-seq or scRNA-seq data is visible, and no code repository is cited.

novelty_literature.justification: The work extends prior TET genomic landscape studies (Petrini 2014; Radovich 2018) with a genuinely novel integrative framework: (i) a three-subgroup molecular classification (GTF2I-type, CN-type, thymic carcinoma) anchored to cross-species single-cell cell-of-origin mapping; (ii) identification of IRS4 transcriptional activation as a putative CN-type oncogenic driver with functional validation and prognostic signal; and (iii) chromosomal amplification-timing analysis suggesting CN-type thymomas initiate early in life. Novelty is partially constrained because GTF2I hotspots, APOBEC in thymic carcinoma, tuft-cell resemblance of thymic carcinoma (Yamada 2021), and GTF2I-impaired TEP differentiation (Giorgetti 2022; He 2022) were previously reported, so the paper is best characterized as a strong empirical and conceptual synthesis rather than a first-in-class discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear narrative arc from genomic subgrouping to cell-of-origin inference, pathway analysis, mutational timing, IRS4 functional validation, and immune profiling. The abstract is self-contained and quantitatively grounded (cohort sizes, three subgroups, specific drivers), figure captions are detailed and standalone-interpretable, and methods subheadings are logically ordered. Minor issues include duplication of the one-sentence summary at the top and bottom of the abstract, dense result paragraphs with many parenthetical p-values that could be tightened, and inconsistent nomenclature between GTF2I L404H and L424H across references, which could confuse readers.

key_strengths: Integrative multiomic design combining 137 TETs (20 new + 117 TCGA) with cross-species single-cell TEC atlases and independent single-cell/spatial validation cohorts
Novel three-subgroup molecular classification with concordant genomic, transcriptomic, metabolic, and immune signatures

Identification and functional validation of IRS4 as a putative CN-type oncogenic driver with prognostic significance independent of Masaoka stage, plus demonstrated resistance to IGF1R inhibitor linsitinib
Mutational-timing analysis using coamplified point mutations providing novel evolutionary insight (early-life initiation of CN-type thymomas)
Clinically actionable immune-checkpoint findings nominating CTLA4/CD80-CD86 and IDO1 pathways over PD-1/PD-L1 in TETs
key_concerns: IRS4 functional validation restricted to HEK293T cells rather than thymoma-relevant models; small WGS cohort (n=5) underpowering timing claims
Post hoc IRS4 >30 TPM dichotomy for survival without an independent validation cohort for the cutoff
No explicit data-availability statement for new SNUH sequencing data or code repository; incomplete STROBE/REMARK adherence (no flow diagram, no sample-size justification, pre-specification unclear)
Inconsistent GTF2I mutation nomenclature (L404H vs L424H) across the manuscript and cited references
Limited exploration of mechanisms underlying IRS4 activation (speculated epigenetic but not tested)
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically solid, well-written integrative multiomic study of a rare tumor with meaningful translational hypotheses and strong validation, but functional work is limited to a non-thymoma cell line and the classification is an extension rather than a paradigm shift, placing it comfortably at Tier 2 with minor revisions.
